entries.what_happened: The manuscript 'Global classical solutions of the three-dimensional relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system' (the only manuscript in this family) claims global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions of the one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system in three space and three momentum dimensions, for every smooth admissible datum (Theorem 1.1, thm:global). A datum is a nonnegative smooth particle density f0 with compact support, and fields E0, B0 with all spatial derivatives bounded and finite energy, satisfying the two Gauss constraints (div E0 = rho of f0, div B0 = 0). Nonzero total charge is allowed. For each finite T the solution has f smooth on [0,T] x R^3 x R^3, E and B smooth on [0,T] x R^3, f with compact phase-space support on [0,T], and the constraints hold for all time. The proof has two parts. (i) A signed momentum-increment estimate along characteristics (Proposition 1.1, eq. bootstrap): |V_X(t2) - V_X(t1)| <= M P sqrt(t2 - t1) + A (t2 - t1) S(w), with S(w) = P^2 log(2+P)/w, proved by a bootstrap and continuity argument (setup.tex, direction.tex, selection.tex, closure.tex). Since the resulting lower bounds on the time needed to double the maximal momentum have a divergent sum, finite-time growth of momentum is excluded. (ii) A local-theory and bounded-momentum continuation statement (Proposition 1.2, continuation.tex). The manuscript obtains it from the Glassey–Strauss criterion as quoted by Luk and Strain, after a finite-horizon modification of the initial fields: the Coulomb field is kept and a vacuum Maxwell solution vanishing on the particle region is subtracted.
entries.delivers: Global existence, uniqueness and smoothness on each finite time interval for the relativistic one-species Vlasov–Maxwell system in three space dimensions, with no restriction on size, symmetry or total charge. The restrictions that come with it: (a) the initial particle density must be smooth and compactly supported, so noncompact particle data are not covered; (b) the fields must have all spatial derivatives bounded and finite energy (in L^2), so fields without finite energy are not covered; (c) uniqueness holds only in the class of classical solutions as the manuscript defines it (C^1 solutions with E, B continuous into L^2); (d) the bound on the momentum support is available on each finite interval only and may grow with that interval; (e) the equations are written in a normalization with the usual 4 pi absorbed into the fields and charge density. The manuscript says the result 'resolves the large-data global classical regularity problem for this model'. Its own statement of the problem is narrower than the list's wording: it concerns the one-species relativistic system, compactly supported initial particles and finite-energy fields, whereas the list's bullet names no species, no relativistic or classical variant, and no data class. The manuscript says nothing about the non-relativistic, multi-species or radiation-reaction variants.
entries.remains: If the manuscript is correct, these parts of the problem are not addressed: (i) particle data that are not compactly supported (the introduction notes that Bigorgne and Wang treat noncompact particle data, but only under smallness, and Wang's 2026 result handles noncompact data only for cylindrically symmetric large data with H^s fields and a weighted density); (ii) field data outside finite energy, or fields whose derivatives are not all bounded; (iii) other variants of the system: multi-species, non-relativistic, other spatial dimensions, radiation reaction, and weaker solution classes; (iv) bounds that are uniform in time, since the manuscript proves momentum and regularity bounds only on each finite interval.
entries.direction: proves global regularity (existence, uniqueness, smoothness on finite intervals) for a restricted data class
entries.conditional_on: The theorem itself assumes nothing beyond the datum class. The proof relies on the Glassey–Strauss bounded-momentum continuation criterion in the form quoted by Luk and Strain (their Theorem 1.1 and Footnote 1, arXiv version). The manuscript applies this criterion to its modified data (continuation.tex, 'The bounded-momentum criterion') and does not prove it. The retarded-field and characteristic-change formulas are attributed to Glassey–Strauss, Luk–Strain, Pallard and Lazarovici; the text says it derives them again in its own normalization. As far as the text shows, it depends on no other OpenAI manuscript for any step; its citation of Wang's 2026 papers is for comparison.
entries.doubts: The argument is long, and the text itself abbreviates several steps. The small-sector sigma partition is 'omitted' (direct.tex near the small-sector definition; occupation.tex lines 90-93). The justification of differentiation at the cone tip rests on a short argument with the 'omitted potential and cutoff errors' and 'omitted kernel integrals' bounded in a few sentences (retarded.tex lines 268-278). A 'deficit exception' in the spatial-transition lemma is disposed of in one paragraph (selection.tex lines 387-393), and one case in direct.tex (around line 239) is 'omitted'. The key selection lemma (sel:exponents) is an exponent-bookkeeping argument with fixed decimal constants (epsilon = 10^-5, beta = 1.16) and thresholds, and the text presents it as exact without any computer check. The abstract's 'arbitrary smooth admissible initial data' is qualified by the definition of admissible data (compact particle support, finite-energy fields). The abstract's 'resolves the large-data global classical regularity problem for this model' is stronger than the list's wording. The text is an unsigned preprint attributed to 'OpenAI', and it does not say it has been reviewed.
